# feat: xRegistry message integration

## Overview

Connect the CLI to the read-only xRegistry so `int create --subscribe
<message-ref>` wires a component to an external CloudEvents stream in one
flag, add a `message` noun for discovery, and unify internal and external
events under one vocabulary — **message** — with two resolution sources:
the registry (external) and the system's producer components (internal).
The `contract`/`topic` flat wiring keys are superseded by `subscribe` /
`publishes` blocks, read leniently during transition.

---

## Problem Frame

See origin: docs/brainstorms/2026-09-04-xregistry-message-integration-requirements.md.
Wiring values the registry already owns (CloudEvents type, pubsub, topic,
schema) are today typed by hand into template prompts, and intra-system
events are described by a different vocabulary (`contract` = C# type name
in the shared contract project) than cross-system events.

---

## Requirements Trace

- R1. `--subscribe` resolves ref → pubsub/topic/CE type via producing endpoint channel
- R2. Scaffold record stores `subscribe: {message, pubsub, topic, dataschema, dataschemaurl}`, list-growable shape
- R3. Block records logical `dataschema` (xid) and pinned `dataschemaurl` (version URL)
- R4. `--subscribe` against a template with no message parameters is a usage error
- R5. `message list` / `message show <ref>`, external + internal
- R6. `message list --group <id>` filter
- R7. Interactive pick list for message parameters when `--subscribe` absent
- R8. `contract` → `message` rename across values, topology, user text
- R9. Internal messages producer-declared via `publishes: {message, dataschema?}`
- R10. Assembly aggregates internal messagegroup; resolves subscriber channel from producer
- R11. `sys create/update` never contacts the registry
- R12. `registryUrl` config key + context override + `--registry-url`, no default
- R13. Degradation contract (unconfigured vs unreachable; hard fail vs fallback)

**Origin actors:** A1 (integration developer), A2 (external codegen tool), A3 (xRegistry service)
**Origin flows:** F1 (subscribe external), F2 (discover), F3 (internal wiring), F4 (codegen)
**Origin acceptance examples:** AE1 (covers R1–R3), AE2 (covers R4), AE3 (covers R13), AE4 (covers R9, R10)

---

## Scope Boundaries

- No code generation in the CLI; no `schema` noun or schema-fetch command
- No multiple subscriptions per component; no registry writes; no internal→external promotion flow
- No record migration tooling — dual-read only
- Filtering beyond `--group` deferred; no `message` verbs beyond `list`/`show`

### Deferred to Follow-Up Work

- Template library changes (loader/extractor/system-host templates declare message parameters and render the internal messagegroup): separate PR in the templates repo. The CLI units here land behind dual-read and work with current template releases; end-to-end `--subscribe` requires the template PR.
- Host SDK / `graph` verb emitting the messagegroup section of the topology record: templates/host repo.
- Future `int update`-style re-resolve of `subscribe` blocks against the registry.

---

## Context & Research

### Relevant Code and Patterns

- `internal/config/config.go` — `Config`/`Context`/`Flags` layering with env fallbacks (`INTROPY_TEMPLATE_REPO` is the pattern for `INTROPY_REGISTRY_URL`); `Resolve` order flags → env → context → file
- `internal/registry/` — the OCI HTTP client: construction via functional options, `UserAgent` injection, typed error mapping. The new xregistry client mirrors this shape; the two packages share a name and nothing else, so the new package is `internal/xregistry` with a doc comment disowning the relation
- `internal/template/wiring.go` — the CLI-owned wiring vocabulary constants; the one home for new keys
- `internal/template/facts.go`, `suggest.go`, `values.go` — workspace facts: prefill on single candidate, pick-list suggestions on several, `ContractFor` conflict demotion
- `internal/template/prompt.go` — `StdinPrompter` suggestion lists accept free input alongside picks; `internal/interactive/select.go` for richer selection
- `internal/system/assemble.go`, `blocks.go`, `model.go`, `payload.go` — assembly: `blockParsers` registry, strict `RecordValue` regime, topic-contract conflict errors, first-seen-wins dedup
- `internal/system/update.go` (`mergeWiring`, ~line 337) — re-injects wiring values on update; must learn the new block shape
- `internal/topology/topology.go` — topology record decode; opaque passthrough precedent (`APIs []json.RawMessage`) for sections whose shape is not finalized
- `cmd/intropy/int_list.go` — table via `text/tabwriter`, `--output json` to stdout, empty state on stderr (`no releases found` style)
- `cmd/intropy/flagtext.go` — shared flag description constants (AGENTS.md requires one for any shared flag)
- `cmd/intropy/int_create.go` — `-n` as sugar for `--set name=` is the precedent for `--subscribe` seeding values before resolution
- `internal/system/create.go` (`requireFactsPayload`) — precedent for gating on template-release capability

### Institutional Learnings

- No `docs/solutions/` directory exists yet — nothing to carry forward.

### External References

- intropy-registry `docs/api.md` and `registry/` definitions (sibling repo): endpoint `channel` is `<pubsub>/<topic>`; endpoints carry `usage: [producer]`; messages carry `dataschemaxid`; schema Version URLs are immutable; `/export` inlines all collections
- xRegistry 1.0-rc4 spec — only the served subset matters; the client must not invent endpoints the registry declares out of scope (filtering/inlining query params)

---

## Key Technical Decisions

- **Client consumes `/export`, not per-entity walks**: one GET yields every message, group, endpoint, and schema; the registry guarantees it byte-identical to the entity paths. Resolution (message → producer endpoint → channel) happens in-memory. Per-entity fetches stay available for `message show` freshness but are not required for v1.
- **Dual-read, never dual-write**: new scaffolds write only the `subscribe`/`publishes` block shape; readers (facts, assembly, suggestions, `mergeWiring`) accept both the blocks and the legacy flat `topic`/`contract`/`pubsub` keys. No rewrite of existing records; the legacy path dies when template releases stop emitting it.
- **`contract` semantics preserved through the rename**: today's `contract` value is a .NET type name in the shared contract project, not a CloudEvents type. The internal message block therefore carries `message` (name, doubles as the CE type) alongside the existing contract-type value during transition; the messagegroup payload to the host template keeps both fields so current host templates keep rendering. Folding the .NET type fully into the message model is template-repo work.
- **Subscriber channel resolution moves to assembly**: internal `subscribe` blocks name only the message; `Assemble` resolves pubsub/topic from the component whose `publishes` declares that message. External `subscribe` blocks carry their own snapshot and need no producer.
- **Unresolved internal subscription is a hard assembly error** naming the message and the subscribing record — a half-wired system must not render (mirrors `parseTransactional`'s both-ports-required rule).
- **Ambiguous producer resolution**: interactive runs offer a pick list of candidate channels; `--no-input` fails listing the candidates. Same rule for several producer endpoints on one message group and for a message group with no producer endpoint (error names the group).
- **`dataschemaurl` pins the schema's default version at subscribe time**; the version ID is recoverable from the URL. Re-pinning is the future re-resolve flow, not v1.
- **`--no-input` + required message parameter + no `--subscribe` fails** naming `--subscribe` — consistent with the flag's "fail rather than ask" contract.

---

## Open Questions

### Resolved During Planning

- Migration path for existing records: dual-read, no tooling (see Key Technical Decisions).
- Subscriber names an unpublished internal message: hard assembly error.
- Multiple producer endpoints, different channels: interactive pick; `--no-input` error listing candidates.
- `message list` internal source: workspace facts scan of scaffold records (works pre-assembly; consistent with prompt suggestions).
- `dataschemaurl` pinning: default version at subscribe time.

### Deferred to Implementation

- Exact `subscribe`/`publishes` block key names inside values (e.g. whether the CE type lives under `message` or a separate `type` key) — settle against the template repo's parameter naming when the first template declares them.
- Whether `message show` hits `/export` or the per-entity path — whichever the client already has; do not add an endpoint for cosmetics.
- Cache policy for `/export` (none vs short-lived) — measure against the local dev registry first; correctness never depends on cache.

---

## High-Level Technical Design

> *This illustrates the intended approach and is directional guidance for review, not implementation specification. The implementing agent should treat it as context, not code to reproduce.*

Resolution flow for `--subscribe` (F1):

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[int create --subscribe REF] --> B[xregistry client: GET /export]
    B --> C{resolve REF}
    C -->|message + group| D[find endpoint: usage=producer, messagegroups contains group]
    D -->|exactly 1| E[split channel pubsub/topic]
    D -->|several| F[pick list, or error under --no-input]
    D -->|none| G[error naming group]
    E --> H[resolve dataschemaxid -> schema default version URL]
    H --> I[seed values: subscribe block]
    I --> J[template.Resolve as today]
```

Record shape written into `.intropy/scaffold.json` values:

```jsonc
{
  "subscribe": {
    "message": "io.intropy.maxbo.product.export",
    "pubsub": "product-distribution-pubsub",
    "topic": "sbt-test-product-extractor-001",
    "dataschema": "/schemagroups/io.intropy.maxbo.product/schemas/product-export.v1",
    "dataschemaurl": "https://registry.intropy.io/schemagroups/io.intropy.maxbo.product/schemas/product-export.v1/versions/1"
  }
}
```

Internal publisher (R9): `"publishes": {"message": "product-exported", "contract": "ProductExported"}` —
`contract` kept during transition for the .NET shared-project type.

---

## Implementation Units

- [ ] U1. **xregistry client package**

**Goal:** Read-only client for the registry with in-memory resolution of message refs to wiring.

**Requirements:** R1, R3, and the resolution half of R13

**Dependencies:** None

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/xregistry/client.go`, `internal/xregistry/types.go`, `internal/xregistry/resolve.go`
- Test: `internal/xregistry/client_test.go`, `internal/xregistry/resolve_test.go`

**Approach:**
- Package doc comment states it is unrelated to `internal/registry` (OCI) — they share a name and nothing else
- Functional-options construction, `UserAgent`, context-first methods, mirroring `internal/registry/client.go`
- `Export(ctx)` GETs `/export`; typed decode of messagegroups/messages (attributes on the default version), endpoints (`usage`, `channel`, `messagegroups`), schemagroups/schemas (versions, `defaultversionid`)
- `ResolveMessage(ref)` → resolved wiring: message, CE type from `envelopemetadata.type.value`, candidate channels from producer endpoints, schema xid + default version URL
- Typed errors: message not found, no producer endpoint, ambiguous producers (carrying candidates), schema not found — callers map them to the CLI error voice
- Channel split helper `<pubsub>/<topic>` rejecting malformed channels

**Test scenarios:**
- Happy path: export fixture with one producer endpoint → resolved wiring carries pubsub, topic, CE type, dataschema xid, pinned `/versions/<default>` URL (Covers AE1's resolution half)
- Happy path: message attributes read from the default version, not the message resource
- Edge case: message ref that matches no message → `MessageNotFound` naming the ref
- Edge case: group with no producer endpoint → error naming the group
- Edge case: two producer endpoints with different channels → ambiguous error listing both channels
- Edge case: malformed channel (no `/`, empty half) → error naming the endpoint
- Error path: non-200 from registry → wrapped error naming the operation; xRegistry error body surfaced
- Error path: unreachable host → context/transport error wrapped, not panicked
- Integration: httptest server serving a captured `/export` document → end-to-end resolve

**Verification:**
- `go test ./internal/xregistry/` green; package docs explain the resolution join in the AGENTS.md comment style

---

- [ ] U2. **Registry URL configuration**

**Goal:** `registryUrl` flows from file/context/env/flag to any command that needs it.

**Requirements:** R12, and the unconfigured half of R13

**Dependencies:** None

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/config/config.go`
- Modify: `cmd/intropy/flagtext.go` (add `flagUsageRegistryURL` constant)
- Test: `internal/config/config_test.go`

**Approach:**
- Add `RegistryUrl` to `Config`, `Context`, `Flags`; env `INTROPY_REGISTRY_URL`; `Resolve` layering identical to `TemplateRepo`
- No built-in default; empty means unconfigured
- Flag description constant: fragment style, names the config key and env var as defaults, per `flagUsageTemplateRepo` precedent

**Test scenarios:**
- Happy path: file value resolved; context override beats file; flag beats context; env beats file
- Edge case: empty everywhere → resolved empty (unconfigured), no error at load
- Error path: unknown config key still rejected (existing strictness preserved with the new key accepted)

**Verification:**
- `go test ./internal/config/` green; `intropy <cmd> --help` shows the shared description wherever the flag lands

---

- [ ] U3. **Wiring vocabulary: subscribe/publishes blocks + dual-read**

**Goal:** New keys and block parsing in `internal/template`, with facts/suggestions reading both shapes.

**Requirements:** R2, R8, R9; enables R7, R10

**Dependencies:** None (block shape settled in plan; U1 not required)

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/template/wiring.go`, `internal/template/facts.go`, `internal/template/suggest.go`, `internal/template/values.go`
- Test: `internal/template/facts_test.go`, `internal/template/suggest_test.go`, `internal/template/wiring_test.go` (new)

**Approach:**
- New constants: `KeySubscribe`, `KeyPublishes`, `KeyMessage`, `KeyDataschema`, `KeyDataschemaURL`; legacy `KeyTopic`/`KeyContract`/`KeyPubsub` retained
- Strict reader for the `subscribe` map (RecordValue-equivalent regime: present-but-mistyped is an error naming the record); soft reader for suggestions
- Facts index gains message-keyed views: internal messages from `publishes` blocks, topics from both new and legacy shapes; `ContractFor` demotion logic preserved for legacy records
- Writers never emit legacy keys

**Test scenarios:**
- Happy path: record with `subscribe` block → strict reader yields message/pubsub/topic/dataschema/dataschemaurl
- Happy path: legacy flat-key record → same reader yields equivalent wiring (dual-read)
- Edge case: block present but `pubsub` mistyped → error naming record and key
- Edge case: block and legacy keys both present → block wins, no error
- Edge case: facts over mixed old/new workspace → suggestions union without duplicates
- Error path: empty `message` in block → error naming the record

**Verification:**
- `go test ./internal/template/` green; no call site writes legacy keys

---

- [ ] U4. **`message` noun: list and show**

**Goal:** Human/agent discovery surface for external and internal messages.

**Requirements:** R5, R6, R13 (degradation)

**Dependencies:** U1, U2, U3

**Files:**
- Create: `cmd/intropy/message.go`, `cmd/intropy/message_list.go`, `cmd/intropy/message_show.go`
- Test: `cmd/intropy/message_test.go` (or per-command test files, repo convention)

**Approach:**
- `message list [--group <id>] [--output json]`: registry messages merged with workspace internal messages (facts scan); table via `text/tabwriter` (ref, group, channel, schema), one row per message; empty state on stderr lowercase (`no messages found`)
- `message show <ref> [--output json]`: one message's definition — envelope metadata, channel, producing endpoint, schema refs; internal refs resolve from workspace facts
- `--registry-url` flag using the U2 constant; unconfigured → usage error naming `registryUrl` and the config path; unreachable → wrapped error front-loading what failed
- Help text per AGENTS.md: one-line imperative `Short`, `Long` ≤150 words, registry reading described in one sentence

**Test scenarios:**
- Happy path: list against fixture registry → rows grouped, `--group` narrows to one group (Covers F2)
- Happy path: list inside a workspace with `publishes` records → internal messages appear, marked as local
- Happy path: `--output json` emits machine-readable document on stdout, diagnostics on stderr
- Edge case: empty registry + no workspace → `no messages found` on stderr, exit 0
- Error path: unconfigured registry → error names `registryUrl` and how to set it (Covers AE3)
- Error path: unreachable registry → error front-loads the failure; stderr only
- Error path: `show` with unknown ref → not-found naming the ref

**Verification:**
- `go test ./cmd/intropy/` green; `intropy message list --help` passes the helptext conventions test

---

- [ ] U5. **`int create --subscribe`**

**Goal:** One-flag external subscription with resolution, prompting, and record write.

**Requirements:** R1, R2, R3, R4, R7, R13

**Dependencies:** U1, U2, U3

**Files:**
- Modify: `cmd/intropy/int_create.go`
- Modify: `internal/template/create.go` (seed resolved block into values pre-resolution), `internal/template/prepare.go` as needed
- Test: `cmd/intropy/int_create_test.go`, `internal/template/create_test.go`

**Approach:**
- `--subscribe <ref>` resolves via U1 before value resolution, seeds the `subscribe` block like `-n` seeds `name`; `--registry-url` override flag
- Usage error when the template declares no message parameters (R4) — checked against the fetched template manifest before any render (Covers AE2)
- Interactive: template message parameter without `--subscribe` prompts with pick list from registry + facts (U3 readers); pick list keeps the free-text escape per `promptSuggestedList`
- Registry unreachable during prompting: warn on stderr, fall back to facts-only suggestions; during explicit `--subscribe`: fail hard
- `--no-input` + missing required message parameter → error naming `--subscribe`
- Record written with the block shape from U3 (Covers AE1)

**Test scenarios:**
- Happy path: Covers AE1 — subscribe against fixture registry writes the full block, no prompts for wired values
- Happy path: pick-list prompt offers registry messages plus local internal messages
- Error path: Covers AE2 — non-message template + `--subscribe` → usage error naming the template
- Error path: unconfigured registry + `--subscribe` → remediation error (Covers AE3)
- Error path: unreachable registry + `--subscribe` → hard failure; same during prompting → stderr warning + facts fallback
- Error path: `--no-input` without `--subscribe` → error naming the flag
- Edge case: ambiguous producers → interactive pick; `--no-input` → error listing candidate channels

**Verification:**
- `go test ./cmd/intropy/ ./internal/template/` green; scaffold record on disk matches the U3 shape

---

- [ ] U6. **Assembly: producer-declared internal messages**

**Goal:** `sys create/update` understands both wiring shapes, aggregates the internal messagegroup, and resolves subscriber channels from producers.

**Requirements:** R9, R10, R11; R8 in system code

**Dependencies:** U3

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/system/blocks.go`, `internal/system/assemble.go`, `internal/system/model.go`, `internal/system/payload.go`, `internal/system/update.go` (`mergeWiring`)
- Test: `internal/system/assemble_test.go`, `internal/system/update_test.go`, `internal/system/payload_test.go`

**Approach:**
- `parseTopicBlock` accepts the block shape via U3 readers; legacy path untouched
- Component model distinguishes publish vs subscribe wiring; subscriber `subscribe{message}` (internal, no channel) resolves against the workspace's `publishes` declarations — external subscriptions carry their own snapshot (R11: no network here)
- Legacy records are directionless (shared topic key pairs the halves); their publish/subscribe direction is derived from block kind (extractor publishes, loader subscribes) — the same rule the host template applies today — so mixed workspaces assemble deterministically
- `Assemble` gains cross-component checks: subscriber names unpublished message → hard error naming message + record (Covers AE4's failure twin); two producers publish the same message → conflict error in the existing topic-conflict style
- Model/payload gain the internal messagegroup section (name + type required, `dataschema` optional, `contract` carried for the .NET type during transition); `mergeWiring` round-trips the new shape
- Assembly never builds an xregistry client (R11) — enforce by construction: no import

**Test scenarios:**
- Happy path: Covers AE4 — publisher + subscriber records assemble; subscriber's channel resolves from the publisher; payload's messagegroup contains the message with its type
- Happy path: external `subscribe` block assembles from its snapshot with the registry unreachable (R11)
- Happy path: mixed legacy + new records assemble into one system
- Edge case: legacy topic-conflict check still fires for conflicting contracts on one topic key
- Error path: subscriber names unpublished message → error naming message and record
- Error path: two producers, same message → conflict error naming both paths
- Integration: `sys update` on a mixed workspace re-renders wiring without dropping block values (mergeWiring round-trip)

**Verification:**
- `go test ./internal/system/` green; no `internal/xregistry` import under `internal/system/`

---

- [ ] U7. **Topology record + vocabulary docs**

**Goal:** The topology model carries the internal messagegroup shape, and user-facing vocabulary docs catch up with the rename.

**Requirements:** R8, R10 (topology half)

**Dependencies:** U3, U6

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/topology/topology.go` (messagegroup section; opaque decode per the `APIs` precedent if the host shape is not yet final)
- Modify: `AGENTS.md` (vocabulary section: `message` definition, `event` as prose, `message` noun verbs), `cmd/intropy/flagtext.go` if new shared flags landed
- Modify: `catalog/concepts/intropy-resource-model.md` and related concept docs mentioning `contract`
- Test: `internal/topology/topology_test.go`

**Approach:**
- Decode the messagegroup section leniently: preserve for round-trip to the dashboard without asserting an unfinalized schema (the `APIs []json.RawMessage` precedent)
- Docs rename `contract` → `message` where the concept means the message definition; keep `contract` only where the .NET shared project is literally meant, marked as transitional

**Test scenarios:**
- Happy path: topology record with messagegroup section decodes and re-encodes losslessly
- Edge case: record without the section (older hosts) decodes identically to today
- Test expectation for docs: none — prose only

**Verification:**
- `go test ./internal/topology/` green; `grep -rn "contract" catalog/` shows only transitional mentions

---

## System-Wide Impact

- **Interaction graph:** value resolution (`values.go`), prompt suggestions (`suggest.go`), assembly (`blocks.go`/`assemble.go`), and `mergeWiring` all read wiring — U3's dual-read is the single seam every consumer shares; no consumer may parse blocks ad hoc.
- **Error propagation:** xregistry errors are typed at the client boundary and mapped to the CLI error voice at the command layer (front-loaded failure, remediation on the second line); assembly errors keep the strict `RecordValue` regime.
- **State lifecycle risks:** scaffold records are committed files — dual-read prevents a mixed fleet of old and new records from breaking any command; writers emit new shape only.
- **API surface parity:** the dashboard (`internal/dashboard`, `web/`) renders template fields and wiring; it reads the same facts/scaffold shapes and will show `subscribe` blocks — parity work there is follow-up, not this plan.
- **Integration coverage:** end-to-end `--subscribe` requires the template-repo PR (see Deferred to Follow-Up Work); CLI units are tested against fixtures until then.
- **Unchanged invariants:** the OCI release/template registry (`internal/registry`, `release`, `template` nouns) is untouched; `sys create/update` stays offline; legacy flat-key records remain fully functional.

---

## Risks & Dependencies

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| Template library lags the CLI, so `--subscribe` errors on every current template (R4) | Dual-read keeps everything else working; template PR is sequenced immediately after; R4 error message points at the required template release |
| `contract` means two things during transition (CE type vs .NET type) | Both fields carried in the messagegroup payload; docs mark the .NET usage transitional; full fold-in is template-repo work |
| Registry `channel` format changes (`<pubsub>/<topic>`) | Split helper validates and errors naming the endpoint; registry conformance suite owns the format |
| `/export` grows large as the registry grows | One GET per command invocation; cache policy deferred to implementation with correctness never cache-dependent |
| Registry unavailable in CI/offline demos | R11 keeps assembly offline; `message`/`--subscribe` failures carry remediation; local dev registry via `task dev` in intropy-registry |

---

## Documentation / Operational Notes

- AGENTS.md vocabulary section updated in U7 — the house style file is the authority contributors read.
- `catalog/concepts/` gains the message-model explanation; the xRegistry relationship links to intropy-registry's `docs/api.md`.
- No rollout concerns: CLI is opt-in per release; new keys are additive to scaffold records.

---

## Sources & References

- **Origin document:** docs/brainstorms/2026-09-04-xregistry-message-integration-requirements.md
- Related code: `internal/template/wiring.go`, `internal/system/assemble.go`, `internal/config/config.go`, `internal/registry/client.go`
- External docs: intropy-registry `docs/api.md` (sibling repo), xRegistry 1.0-rc4 spec

+---
+type: Intropy Concept
+title: Messages and subscriptions
+description: How internal and external messages, subscribes, and publishes relate.
+tags: [intropy, concepts, messaging]
+status: draft
+commands:
+  - intropy message list
+  - intropy message show
+  - intropy int create --subscribe
+sources:
+  - id: xregistry-api
+    resource: https://registry.intropy.io
+    title: Intropy xRegistry API reference
+  - id: xregistry-spec
+    resource: https://xregistry.io
+    title: xRegistry specification
+---
+
+# Purpose
+
+<!-- One paragraph: wiring values the registry already owns (CloudEvents type,
+pubsub, topic, schema) were typed by hand into template prompts; internal
+events used a different vocabulary than cross-system events. One formal
+vocabulary — message — replaces both. -->
+
+# Concepts
+
+| Concept | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| Message | A message definition. Comes from the read-only xRegistry (external) or a producing component's `publishes` block (internal). |
+| Subscribe | Written into a component's record as a `subscribe` block. An internal block names only the message; assembly resolves its channel from the producer. An external block carries the full snapshot (pubsub, topic, dataschema, pinned schema version URL). |
+| Publishes | A producer's declaration: `message` (doubles as the CloudEvents type) plus the transitional `contract` (the .NET shared-project type name). |
+| Channel | `<pubsub>/<topic>` — producer-declared on the registry, resolved from the publisher in assembly for internal subscriptions. |
+
+# Invariants
+
+- `sys create`/`sys update` never contact the registry; external
+  subscriptions carry their own snapshot.
+- Records written today use the block shape only. Legacy flat
+  `topic`/`contract`/`pubsub` records stay functional and read as
+  `publishes`/`subscribe` derived from the block kind (extractor publishes,
+  loader subscribes).
+- An internal subscription whose message no component publishes is an
+  assembly error, not a rendered half-wired system.
+- `dataschemaurl` pins the schema's default version at subscribe time;
+  re-pinning is a future re-resolve flow.
+
+# Examples
+
+<!-- Show: message list output, one subscribe block in a scaffold record,
+one publishes block, and the resulting messagegroup in the topology. -->
+
+# Related knowledge
+
+- [Intropy resource model](/concepts/intropy-resource-model.md)
+- [State and ownership](/concepts/state-and-ownership.md)

**Verdict: needs changes** — the implementation is faithful to the plan across all seven units and the full test suite is green, but two behavioral defects in the `--subscribe`/prompt flow should be fixed before merge, plus a handful of low-severity residuals.

## Findings

### Medium

**1. `--subscribe` does not satisfy the template's declared message parameter — and the failure's remediation names the flag already passed**
- `internal/template/create.go` (~line 196): `opts.SetValues[KeySubscribe] = SubscribeBlockValue(opts.Subscribe)` seeds only the `subscribe` key. The manifest's `intropy.dev/message-params` parameter (e.g. `message`) stays unresolved.
- Consequence A: `int create msg-loader --subscribe <ref> --no-input` against a message-capable template with `required: [message]` fails `missing required parameter(s): message`, and `missingRequiredError` (`internal/template/values.go:270`) appends `pass --subscribe <message-ref> to wire the message parameter…` — telling the user to do what they just did. Plan: U5 test scenario "`--no-input` without `--subscribe` → error naming the flag"; the hint is correct only when `--subscribe` is absent.
- Consequence B: interactive runs prompt for the `message` parameter even after `--subscribe` resolved it, against AE1's "no prompts for wired values".
- Fix: when `opts.Subscribe != nil`, seed the label-declared message parameters with the resolved message ref (the label already names them via `MessageParameters()`), and/or suppress the `--subscribe` hint when `opts.Subscribe` was set.

**2. Every interactive `int create` now GETs `/export` before the template is even fetched**
- `cmd/intropy/int_create.go` (~line 78): `downloadRefs := !noInput && subscribe == ""` triggers `registryMessageRefs` for *any* template whenever a registry is configured. For templates with no message parameters (all current ones), the request is pure waste — and with a configured-but-unreachable registry, every interactive create stalls on the network and prints `warning: … prompt suggestions fall back to workspace messages only` for a feature the template cannot use.
- Fix: fetch candidates after the manifest is fetched, gated on `len(tmpl.MessageParameters()) > 0` — the natural seam is inside `prepareCreateTemplate`, which already registers the params into facts.

### Low

**3. No HTTP timeout on registry calls, and compound exposure from finding 2.**
`internal/xregistry/client.go` doc says "the caller owns timeouts"; no caller sets one (`http.DefaultClient` in `New`). A hung registry blocks interactive create indefinitely. Fix: default `http.Client{Timeout: …}` in `New` unless `WithHTTPClient` overrides.

**4. Stored messagegroup shape drifts between `sys create` and `sys update`.**
`internal/system/payload.go` emits `publisher` for every message; the orphan path in `mergeWiring` (`internal/system/update.go` ~line 407) writes `name`/`type`/`contract`/`dataschema` but never `publisher`. A message first seen via update has a different stored shape than one from create. Fix: add `publisher` to the `mergeWiring` literal.

**5. R9's optional `dataschema` on `publishes` is unimplemented; the emit branches are dead.**
Plan R9 allows `publishes: {message, dataschema?}`, but `PublishesBlock` (`internal/template/wiring.go`) reads only `message`/`contract`, so `MessageWiring.Dataschema` is never set for publishers and the `dataschema` branches in `aggregateMessages`/`buildPayload`/`mergeWiring` are unreachable. Fix: either read an optional `dataschema` in `ReadPublishesBlock`, or drop the dead branches until the template repo needs them.

**6. Residual unused fields / dead tags.**
`ResolvedMessage.Envelope` (`internal/xregistry/resolve.go:66`) is set and never read; the `json:` tags on `ResolvedMessage` and `Channel` are never exercised (nothing marshals them — `MessageEntry` is the output shape). `ResolvedMessage.Type` at least carries a deliberate-keeping comment. Fix: drop `Envelope` and the tags, or document why they stay.

**7. Client construction still triplicated.**
Prior finding partially resolved — `resolveRegistryURL` is shared and the per-entity fetches are gone — but `xregistry.New(url, xregistry.WithUserAgent("intropy-cli/"+version))` appears verbatim at `cmd/intropy/message.go:40`, `int_create.go:240`, `int_create.go:317`. `resolveSubscribeBlock` could call `registryClient()` directly; `registryMessageRefs` needs the non-`Require` variant but could share a constructor helper.

**8. Help-text style nits.**
`flagUsageSubscribe` ("subscribe the component to a registry message…") starts with a verb; AGENTS.md wants noun-first fragments ("registry message reference to wire the component to"). `int create`'s `Long` doesn't mention `--subscribe` at all despite it being the headline flag. `message list`/`show` help text itself passes conventions (verified below).

### Process

**9. Worktree artifacts.** Untracked `docs/brainstorms/` and `docs/plans/` remain in the tree — the release branch history deliberately removed `docs/plans` (commit `706c0a68`), so decide explicitly whether these ship in the PR; never sweep them in with a broad add. The `.gitignore` addition of `/intropy` (built binary) is reasonable hygiene but unrelated to the feature.

## Prior findings re-check

All eight re-checked items are resolved or reduced to the residuals above: prompt-time unconfigured registry is now a silent empty pool (`registryMessageRefs`, covered by `TestRegistryMessageRefsUnconfiguredIsEmpty`); the messagegroup `name`/`message` round-trip is fixed (`payload.go` and `mergeWiring` both write `name`, reader dual-reads with `message` fallback, `TestMergeWiringMessageBlocks`); `--subscribe` maps to `*usageError` via `ErrNoMessageParameters` + `usageIfNoMessageParams` at both call sites (`TestIntCreateSubscribeGateIsUsageError`); dead entity-path fetches are gone (client is `/export`-only, documented in the package comment); `Message.Subscriber` removed; stale comments cleaned.

- The dual-read seam (`HasMessageBlocks` → block wins, never merge) is the single point every consumer shares; the dashboard parity work (explicitly deferred) will be the first new reader and should reuse `ReadSubscribeBlock`/`ReadPublishesBlock` rather than parsing ad hoc.
